index.core_question: What does Imperium Software Technologies do?
index.tldr: Imperium builds AI-powered contact center and customer experience (CX) software — CTI, IVR, omnichannel routing and enterprise telephony — for businesses across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Singapore and India. Its platform runs on established telephony infrastructure (Avaya, Microsoft) alongside cloud partners (AWS, Google Cloud) rather than replacing it, so existing phone systems can be upgraded instead of rebuilt. The goal is fewer channels for customers to repeat themselves across and faster, better-informed responses from agents.
index.how_it_works_heading: How does Imperium's CX platform work?
how_it_works: A customer reaches out by phone, chat, email or social — omnichannel routing brings every channel into one queue instead of separate silos.
CTI (computer telephony integration) matches the contact to existing CRM or customer records and shows the agent that history before they even answer.
AI assists the agent in real time during the interaction, and the call, chat or ticket is logged automatically.
Call and interaction data feeds into reporting so managers can see volume, resolution time and agent performance without pulling records by hand.

faqs.q: What is a contact center?
faqs.a: A contact center is a centralized system for handling customer interactions across every channel — phone, email, chat, social and messaging — rather than just phone calls. It combines routing (getting the contact to the right agent), CTI (showing the agent who's calling and their history) and reporting into one platform.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a call center and a contact center?
faqs.a: A call center handles phone calls only. A contact center handles phone, email, chat, social and messaging through the same routing and reporting system, so an agent sees one unified history regardless of which channel a customer used. Imperium builds contact center platforms, not single-channel call centers.

faqs.q: What is CTI (computer telephony integration)?
faqs.a: CTI links a phone system to a business's software — typically a CRM — so that when a call comes in, the agent's screen automatically shows who's calling and their account or case history, before they say a word. Imperium's CTI module is called CRM Connect.

faqs.q: What is omnichannel customer support, and how is it different from multichannel?
faqs.a: Multichannel means a business offers several contact channels (phone, email, chat) that operate independently, often with separate histories. Omnichannel means those channels are unified — an agent can see a customer's full conversation history regardless of which channel they used last, and a conversation can move between channels without starting over.

faqs.q: Does Imperium offer on-premise or cloud contact center deployments?
faqs.a: Both. Imperium has delivered on-premise Avaya contact center setups (for example, Emirates Hospital Group's centralized call center) and migrated existing on-premise systems to the cloud (Growthgate Capital and Macemacro both moved from on-premise Avaya to cloud-hosted deployments). Which one fits depends on existing infrastructure, compliance requirements and how distributed the business is.

faqs.q: How long does it take to implement contact center software?
faqs.a: It depends on scope — a single-site cloud migration can take a matter of days (Growthgate Capital's migration to Avaya Unified Communications on Cloud was completed in a couple of days, per their IT team), while a multi-branch centralized rollout with custom CTI and reporting, like Emirates Hospital Group's seven-branch setup, is a larger project. See the full case studies for more on both. Talk to Imperium's team for a timeline scoped to your setup.

Each vertical gets the same core platform (CTI, IVR, omnichannel routing, reporting) configured around that industry's specific workflow, from appointment IVR for clinics to policy-aware call routing for insurers.

Businesses outside this list can still be evaluated; contact Imperium's team to discuss a sector not listed here.

Each industry page describes how that platform gets configured for one sector's specific workflow — for example, appointment-booking IVR for healthcare versus shipment-tracking IVR for logistics.

faqs.a: Most of Imperium's deployments combine capabilities from more than one vertical in practice — Concordia (facility management) used help-desk-style call reporting, and Omniyat used real estate lead handling combined with CRM integration and call recording more commonly associated with the finance/insurance pages. Use the industry page closest to your primary workflow as a starting point, then talk to Imperium's team about the specific mix you need.

faqs.a: Compare vendors against your actual call/interaction volume and existing infrastructure (on-premise vs. cloud, which telephony vendor you already run), not just feature lists — ask for a demo scoped to your own scenarios rather than a generic walkthrough, and ask for references in your industry specifically. Imperium's case studies below show the starting problem, what was delivered and the client's own account of the result for exactly this reason.

faqs.a: A useful case study names the client, states the specific problem (not just "they needed better communication"), lists what was actually delivered, and includes the client's own words on the outcome — not just the vendor's claim. Every case study on this page follows that structure and links to the full PDF.

healthcare.core_question: What does a healthcare contact center solution from Imperium include?
healthcare.tldr: Imperium's healthcare contact center software gives hospitals and clinics one system for patient calls, appointment booking and multi-channel support, instead of a separate reception desk per branch or department. It runs on Avaya contact center infrastructure with CTI, so a patient's record appears on the agent's screen before the call even connects, and it can centralize multiple branches behind a single number — as it did for Emirates Hospital Group's seven UAE branches. Imperium has also deployed healthcare-specific modules (SMS gateway, customer surveys) for Al Tadawi Medical Care and Mobile Doctors 24/7.
healthcare.how_it_works_heading: How does Imperium's healthcare contact center work?
how_it_works: A patient calls one number — not a separate line per branch or department — and is routed to the right department by IVR or agent.
CTI (CRM Connect) matches the caller to their existing patient record and shows history on the agent's screen before the call connects.
Appointments can be booked, rescheduled or cancelled through the same system, with every interaction logged for reporting.
Calls that go unanswered past a set wait time can trigger an automatic callback, so an urgent patient query isn't lost in an abandoned queue.

faqs.q: How does IVR work for scheduling patient appointments?
faqs.a: The IVR presents a short menu (for example, book, reschedule, cancel, or speak to a department) so patients can either self-serve an appointment change or reach the right person directly, instead of being routed through a general reception line first.

faqs.q: Can patients reach the right department without waiting on hold?
faqs.a: Routing sends the call directly to the correct department or a skilled agent rather than a single general line. For calls that still go unanswered, Imperium's Callback Assist Module logs the missed call and places an automatic callback, so the patient isn't left to redial and wait again.

faqs.q: How is patient call and appointment data kept secure?
faqs.a: Records are only accessible to authorized agents through the CRM-connected system, rather than being handled on paper or in per-branch spreadsheets. Specific compliance certifications and data-residency requirements vary by health authority — confirm current requirements for your facility directly with Imperium's team.

faqs.q: Can a healthcare contact center handle call spikes without long hold times?
faqs.a: Centralizing branches behind one system (rather than each branch running its own reception) is what let Emirates Hospital Group move away from long call-waiting queues toward a 0% abandoned-call-rate target and a 20-second maximum wait time, with the Callback Assist Module catching whatever still gets missed.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a medical answering service and a full contact center platform?
faqs.a: An answering service typically just takes a message or books a slot. A full platform like Imperium's adds CTI (caller history on-screen), multi-department routing, multi-channel support (voice, email, web chat) and reporting — the same system Emirates Hospital Group used to centralize seven branches, not just a single answering line.

debtcollection.core_question: What does Imperium's debt collection software include?
debtcollection.tldr: Imperium's debt collection software runs on Avaya IP Office and adds predictive dialling, promise-to-pay tracking, full call recording and compliance reporting — built to keep the legally-sensitive interactions debt collectors handle every day auditable and secure. Every call is logged against the customer's account so collectors have a complete history on hand, not a fragmented one across spreadsheets and memory.
debtcollection.how_it_works_heading: How does Imperium's debt collection system work?
how_it_works: Predictive dialling queues and places outbound calls automatically, connecting an agent only once a live person answers.
Every call is recorded and logged against the customer's account, building a complete, searchable interaction history.
Promise-to-pay commitments made on a call are tracked in the system, so a follow-up call happens on schedule instead of being missed.
Reporting tools compile call volume, outcomes and compliance data for supervisors and auditors.

faqs.q: Is predictive dialing legal for debt collectors?
faqs.a: Predictive dialing is a technology, not inherently a legal question — legality depends on your jurisdiction's consent and calling-hours rules for debt collection specifically. Imperium's system supports configurable call-frequency caps and quiet hours so a collections team can operate within whatever rules apply to their market, but confirm current requirements with your own compliance or legal team.

faqs.q: What is "promise-to-pay" tracking, and how does it work?
faqs.a: When a debtor commits to a payment date on a call, that commitment is logged against their account with a due date, so the system (not an agent's memory or a spreadsheet) prompts the follow-up call if the promised payment doesn't come through.

faqs.q: Are debt collection calls recorded, and how long are recordings kept?
faqs.a: Yes — Imperium's system records and logs collection calls automatically against the customer's account. Retention periods should follow your own market's regulatory requirements; Imperium's platform lets you configure retention rather than fixing a single default, since requirements vary by jurisdiction.

faqs.q: What compliance features does debt collection software need?
faqs.a: At minimum: configurable call-frequency limits, quiet-hours enforcement, full call recording, and reporting that can reconstruct exactly what was said and when for any given account — all of which Imperium's platform provides alongside the predictive dialer itself.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a predictive dialer and a regular auto dialer?
faqs.a: An auto dialer simply places calls from a list in sequence. A predictive dialer uses call-answer statistics to dial multiple numbers ahead of agent availability and only connects an agent once a live person picks up, reducing agent idle time between calls.

helpdesk.core_question: What does Imperium's help desk / service desk solution include?
helpdesk.tldr: Imperium's help desk module runs on the Avaya IP Office call center suite and unifies phone, email, chat and social into one ticket queue — so requests get logged, routed and resolved in one place instead of scattered across inboxes and phone lines. It's built for customer service teams that need effective call resolution, not just an internal IT ticketing tool.
helpdesk.how_it_works_heading: How does Imperium's help desk work?
how_it_works: A request comes in by phone, email, chat or social — all channels feed into one ticket queue instead of separate systems.
Tickets are routed to the right agent or team based on the type of request.
The agent resolves the ticket with the customer's history visible, and the resolution is logged.
Reporting shows ticket volume, resolution time and outstanding requests so nothing sits unanswered.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a help desk and a service desk?
faqs.a: A help desk is typically reactive — it exists to log and resolve incoming issues. A service desk is broader, often covering requests and processes beyond just fixing problems. In practice the terms overlap heavily, and Imperium's module covers ticket logging, routing and resolution regardless of which label a business uses.

faqs.q: What's the difference between help desk software and contact center software?
faqs.a: Help desk software centers on ticket tracking — logging a request and resolving it. Contact center software centers on live interaction routing (voice, chat) with CTI and real-time reporting. Imperium's help desk module runs on the same Avaya-based contact center platform, so a business gets both instead of having to run separate systems.

faqs.q: Is a help desk only for IT issues, or can it handle general customer service?
faqs.a: "Help desk" historically meant IT support specifically, but the underlying ticket-logging-and-routing pattern applies to any request queue. Imperium's help desk module is built for the customer service industry generally — logging and resolving customer requests, not just internal IT tickets.

faqs.q: What is omnichannel ticket routing?
faqs.a: It means a ticket opened by phone, email, chat or social all lands in the same queue and gets tracked the same way, rather than each channel having its own separate inbox and history. That's what Imperium's help desk module unifies.

businesscenter.core_question: What does Imperium's business center communication solution include?
businesscenter.tldr: Imperium's business center solution converges voice, video and data onto one multi-tenant telephony system — built for business centers and shared offices where multiple tenant businesses need their own extensions, call reporting and customer engagement tools without each running separate infrastructure.

faqs.q: What is multi-tenant telephony?
faqs.a: It's a single underlying phone/communication system that serves multiple separate businesses (tenants), each with their own extensions, numbers and call data kept isolated from the others — so a business center or shared office can offer real phone infrastructure to every tenant without installing a separate system per company.

faqs.q: Can multiple businesses share one phone system while keeping their calls and extensions separate?
faqs.a: Yes — that's the core of a multi-tenant setup: each tenant gets its own extensions and call reporting, logically separated within the same underlying converged voice/video/data network, rather than one shared, undifferentiated line.

faqs.q: Does this include call reporting per tenant?
faqs.a: Yes — call reporting and omnichannel support are part of the converged solution, so a business center operator (or an individual tenant) can see call activity for their own extensions specifically.

logistics.core_question: What does Imperium's logistics contact center solution include?
logistics.tldr: Imperium's logistics solution uses Avaya IVR with text-to-speech (TTS) so customers can check shipment status, request a new booking or provide a pickup location without waiting in a phone queue or repeating themselves to an agent. Voice input is transcribed to text automatically, and a callback manager lets agents follow up to confirm booking requests captured by the IVR. Imperium has deployed Avaya CCR with IVR integration for courier and logistics clients including Skynet Courier.
logistics.how_it_works_heading: How does Imperium's logistics IVR work?
how_it_works: A customer calls in and the IVR offers self-service options — track a shipment, request a new booking, or provide a pickup/delivery location.
Spoken input (like a tracking number or address) is captured by voice and automatically transcribed to text.
CTI shows the agent the caller's information and case history the moment a call needs a human.
A callback manager downloads booking requests captured by the IVR so agents can call back to confirm details, rather than the customer having to call again.

faqs.q: How does IVR work for tracking a shipment or delivery?
faqs.a: The customer enters or speaks a tracking number through the IVR menu, and the system looks up status without needing an agent — for anything the IVR can't resolve, the call routes to an agent who already has the case details on screen via CTI.

faqs.q: Can delivery status updates be sent automatically instead of the customer having to call in?
faqs.a: Imperium's logistics IVR is built around reducing exactly that pattern — letting customers self-serve a status check by phone rather than needing to reach a live agent for a routine "where is my order" query.

faqs.q: How can a logistics company reduce high call volumes about delivery status?
faqs.a: Self-service IVR for status checks and automated capture of new booking/location requests both take routine queries off agents' queues, so agent time goes to calls that actually need a person — which is the specific gap Imperium's logistics IVR and callback manager address.

faqs.q: Can the contact center system integrate with a company's existing tracking or CRM data?
faqs.a: The IVR is built to pull from a specific database for tracking/status lookups, and CTI connects caller information and case history to the agent's screen — which requires integration with the company's own tracking or CRM system to work; scope that with Imperium's team for your specific setup.

educationsector.core_question: What does Imperium's education sector communication solution include?
educationsector.tldr: Imperium's education sector solution covers admissions IVR, parent notification and student help desk on one platform, so schools, colleges and universities can reach and be reached by a large, dispersed community of students, parents and staff through multiple channels instead of one overloaded reception line. Imperium has deployed this for Al Falah University, Al Ain University and Meric Training Institute.

faqs.q: How does an IVR system work for school or university admissions?
faqs.a: During admissions periods, an IVR menu can route enquiries by topic (application status, document requirements, general information) so a spike in calls doesn't overwhelm a single admissions line, with self-service options handling routine questions.

faqs.q: How can schools handle high call volumes during admissions or exam season?
faqs.a: Routing enquiries through IVR menus and a student/parent help desk system — rather than one general phone line — is what lets an institution absorb a seasonal spike without every call queuing behind the last.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a student help desk and a general IT help desk?
faqs.a: A student help desk in this context covers admissions, enrollment and general student/parent queries — not just technical IT support requests — logged and routed the same way Imperium's help desk module handles any customer service queue.

faqs.q: Can parents be notified automatically rather than the school calling each one individually?
faqs.a: Parent notification is one of the three core pieces of this solution alongside admissions IVR and student help desk — built so notifications go out as a campaign rather than requiring individual outbound calls.

ecommerce.core_question: What does Imperium's e-commerce contact center solution include?
ecommerce.tldr: Imperium's e-commerce solution gives online retailers omnichannel support, order-status IVR and CRM-connected agents, so a customer checking on an order can self-serve through IVR or reach an agent who already sees their order details — without repeating their order number across multiple channels. Imperium has deployed Avaya IPOCC and CRM Connect for online retailers including ELABELZ and Sellanycar.com.
ecommerce.how_it_works_heading: How does Imperium's e-commerce contact center work?
how_it_works: A customer reaches out by phone, chat, email or social about an order — all channels feed into one system.
Order-status IVR lets customers check status by entering an order number, without needing an agent for a routine check.
For anything that needs a person, CTI shows the agent the customer's order and account details before they answer.
Interaction and order data feed back into reporting so the business can see where support volume is actually coming from.

faqs.q: What is IVR and how does it check order status automatically?
faqs.a: The customer enters an order number (or account details) through the IVR menu, and the system looks up status directly — resolving a routine "where's my order" query without tying up an agent.

faqs.q: How does an e-commerce contact center handle high call volumes during sales events?
faqs.a: Order-status IVR absorbs the routine "where's my order" volume that spikes during sales events, so agent time during peak periods goes to queries that actually need a person rather than status checks the IVR can resolve directly.

faqs.q: What's the difference between omnichannel and multichannel support?
faqs.a: Multichannel means offering phone, chat and email as separate, independent options. Omnichannel means those channels share one customer history, so an agent on a chat can see a customer's prior phone call without the customer repeating themselves.

faqs.q: How does CRM integration with a contact center improve customer service?
faqs.a: It's what lets an agent see order and account history the moment they pick up a call or chat, instead of asking the customer to look up and repeat their own order number — which is what Imperium's CTI/CRM-connected agent view is built to do.

realestate.core_question: What does Imperium's real estate communication solution include?
realestate.tldr: Imperium's real estate solution gives brokers and developers real-time, multichannel communication — skill-based call routing, call transfer and recording, and a pop-up of the caller's information the moment a call comes in — so an enquiry doesn't go unanswered or unrouted while a prospective buyer moves on to a competitor. Imperium has deployed CRM Connect and related modules for real estate and property clients including Al Manal Development and Lanteri Australia, alongside Omniyat (see the case studies page).
realestate.how_it_works_heading: How does Imperium's real estate lead-routing work?
how_it_works: A prospective buyer or tenant calls in, and their information (if already in the CRM) pops up on the agent's screen the moment the call connects.
Skill-based routing sends the call to the agent best matched to that enquiry — by property type, price range or existing relationship.
Calls can be transferred and recorded, so a handoff between agents doesn't lose context.
Follow-up happens across voice, video, instant chat and social, connected to the same CRM record — as delivered for Omniyat via Salesforce CRM Connect.

faqs.q: How much does a missed call actually cost a real estate agent or developer?
faqs.a: A missed enquiry often means a prospective buyer simply calls the next listing instead of waiting for a callback — which is the exact gap lead-routing and pop-up caller information are built to close: getting the call to an available, matched agent the first time rather than relying on a callback.

faqs.q: How does lead routing work for real estate teams?
faqs.a: Skill-based routing sends an incoming call to the agent best matched to it — by property type, price range, or an existing relationship in the CRM — rather than to whichever agent happens to be free.

faqs.q: What CRM integration does a real estate brokerage need?
faqs.a: At minimum, the contact center should be able to look up the caller against existing CRM records (so their information pops up automatically) and log the call back into that same CRM. Imperium delivered exactly this for Omniyat, connecting Avaya IP Office Contact Center to their Salesforce CRM.

faqs.q: Can a real estate contact center handle enquiries through social media and chat, not just phone?
faqs.a: Yes — the solution covers voice, video, instant chat and social alongside phone, with call recording for quality/reference purposes.

retail.core_question: What does Imperium's retail customer experience solution include?
retail.tldr: Imperium connects a retailer's stores, contact center and online channels into one view, so an agent handling a customer call can see their purchase history, demographic context and immediate concern in one place — rather than a customer having to explain their situation again to whichever channel they reach. Imperium has deployed this for retail and enterprise clients including Sharaf DG, Konica Minolta and Brother International.

faqs.q: What is omnichannel retail customer service, and how is it different from just having a phone line and a website?
faqs.a: Omnichannel means the contact center, in-store systems and online channels share one customer view — purchase history, prior contacts, demographic context — rather than a phone line and a website operating as two disconnected systems that each start from zero.

faqs.q: How do retailers give store staff and contact center agents the same customer view?
faqs.a: By connecting both to the same CRM/CTI-integrated system, so whichever channel a customer reaches — in-store, phone, chat — the person helping them can see the same account and purchase context.

faqs.q: Can a contact center platform work for both in-store and online customer service?
faqs.a: Yes — that's the specific gap Imperium's retail solution is built to close: unifying store, contact center and online channels rather than treating them as separate systems with separate customer records.

banking.core_question: What does Imperium's banking contact center solution include?
banking.tldr: Imperium's banking solution focuses on secure, authenticated customer engagement — authenticated IVR, call recording, omnichannel servicing and core-banking integration — built on cloud VoIP infrastructure with region-based data hosting, since banks are directly liable for client data and security. faqs.q: How does IVR authentication work for a bank?
